import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
data = pd.read_csv('data/cameras.csv')

# Create a countplot of the different camera brands
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.countplot(x='brand', data=data)
plt.title('Distribution of Camera Brands')
plt.xlabel('Brand')
plt.ylabel('Count')
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output1.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a bar chart of the average price by body type
body_type_avg_price = data.groupby('body_type')['price_usd'].mean().reset_index()
plt.figure(figsize=(8,6))
sns.barplot(x='body_type', y='price_usd', data=body_type_avg_price)
plt.title('Average Price by Body Type')
plt.xlabel('Body Type')
plt.ylabel('Average Price (USD)')
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output2.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Create a scatter plot of megapixels vs price
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.scatterplot(x='megapixels', y='price_usd', data=data)
plt.title('Megapixels vs Price')
plt.xlabel('Megapixels')
plt.ylabel('Price (USD)')
plt.xticks([0, 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, 60])
plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('output3.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
